NASB.1: Then he commanded his house steward, saying, 'Fill the men's sacks with food, as much as they can carry, and put each man's money in the mouth of his sack.
NASB.2: 'Put my cup, the silver cup, in the mouth of the sack of the youngest, and his money for the grain.' And he did as Joseph had told [him].
NASB.3: As soon as it was light, the men were sent away, they with their donkeys.
NASB.4: They had [just] gone out of the city, [and] were not far off, when Joseph said to his house steward, 'Up, follow the men; and when you overtake them, say to them, 'Why have you repaid evil for good?
NASB.5: 'Is not this the one from which my lord drinks and which he indeed uses for divination? You have done wrong in doing this.''
NASB.6: So he overtook them and spoke these words to them.
NASB.7: They said to him, 'Why does my lord speak such words as these? Far be it from your servants to do such a thing.
NASB.8: 'Behold, the money which we found in the mouth of our sacks we have brought back to you from the land of Canaan. How then could we steal silver or gold from your lord's house?
NASB.9: 'With whomever of your servants it is found, let him die, and we also will be my lord's slaves.'
NASB.10: So he said, 'Now let it also be according to your words; he with whom it is found shall be my slave, and [the rest of] you shall be innocent.'
NASB.11: Then they hurried, each man lowered his sack to the ground, and each man opened his sack.
NASB.12: He searched, beginning with the oldest and ending with the youngest, and the cup was found in Benjamin's sack.
NASB.13: Then they tore their clothes, and when each man loaded his donkey, they returned to the city.
NASB.14: When Judah and his brothers came to Joseph's house, he was still there, and they fell to the ground before him.
NASB.15: Joseph said to them, 'What is this deed that you have done? Do you not know that such a man as I can indeed practice divination?'
NASB.16: So Judah said, 'What can we say to my lord? What can we speak? And how can we justify ourselves? God has found out the iniquity of your servants; behold, we are my lord's slaves, both we and the one in whose possession the cup has been found.'
NASB.17: But he said, 'Far be it from me to do this. The man in whose possession the cup has been found, he shall be my slave; but as for you, go up in peace to your father.'
NASB.18: Then Judah approached him, and said, 'Oh my lord, may your servant please speak a word in my lord's ears, and do not be angry with your servant; for you are equal to Pharaoh.
NASB.19: 'My lord asked his servants, saying, 'Have you a father or a brother?'
NASB.20: 'We said to my lord, 'We have an old father and a little child of [his] old age. Now his brother is dead, so he alone is left of his mother, and his father loves him.'
NASB.21: 'Then you said to your servants, 'Bring him down to me that I may set my eyes on him.'
NASB.22: 'But we said to my lord, 'The lad cannot leave his father, for if he should leave his father, his father would die.'
NASB.23: 'You said to your servants, however, 'Unless your youngest brother comes down with you, you will not see my face again.'
NASB.24: 'Thus it came about when we went up to your servant my father, we told him the words of my lord.
NASB.25: 'Our father said, 'Go back, buy us a little food.'
NASB.26: 'But we said, 'We cannot go down. If our youngest brother is with us, then we will go down; for we cannot see the man's face unless our youngest brother is with us.'
NASB.27: 'Your servant my father said to us, 'You know that my wife bore me two sons;
NASB.28: and the one went out from me, and I said, 'Surely he is torn in pieces,' and I have not seen him since.
NASB.29: 'If you take this one also from me, and harm befalls him, you will bring my gray hair down to Sheol in sorrow.'
NASB.30: 'Now, therefore, when I come to your servant my father, and the lad is not with us, since his life is bound up in the lad's life,
NASB.31: when he sees that the lad is not [with us], he will die. Thus your servants will bring the gray hair of your servant our father down to Sheol in sorrow.
NASB.32: 'For your servant became surety for the lad to my father, saying, 'If I do not bring him [back] to you, then let me bear the blame before my father forever.'
NASB.33: 'Now, therefore, please let your servant remain instead of the lad a slave to my lord, and let the lad go up with his brothers.
NASB.34: 'For how shall I go up to my father if the lad is not with me-- for fear that I see the evil that would overtake my father?'

NKJV.1: And he commanded the steward of his house, saying, “Fill the men’s sacks with food, as much as they can carry, and put each man’s money in the mouth of his sack.
NKJV.2: Also put my cup, the silver cup, in the mouth of the sack of the youngest, and his grain money.” So he did according to the word that Joseph had spoken.
NKJV.3: As soon as the morning dawned, the men were sent away, they and their donkeys.
NKJV.4: When they had gone out of the city, and were not yet far off, Joseph said to his steward, “Get up, follow the men; and when you overtake them, say to them, ‘Why have you repaid evil for good?

NKJV.6: So he overtook them, and he spoke to them these same words.
NKJV.7: And they said to him, “Why does my lord say these words? Far be it from us that your servants should do such a thing.
NKJV.8: Look, we brought back to you from the land of Canaan the money which we found in the mouth of our sacks. How then could we steal silver or gold from your lord’s house?
NKJV.9: With whomever of your servants it is found, let him die, and we also will be my lord’s slaves.”
NKJV.10: And he said, “Now also let it be according to your words; he with whom it is found shall be my slave, and you shall be blameless.”
NKJV.11: Then each man speedily let down his sack to the ground, and each opened his sack.
NKJV.12: So he searched. He began with the oldest and left off with the youngest; and the cup was found in Benjamin’s sack.
NKJV.13: Then they tore their clothes, and each man loaded his donkey and returned to the city.
NKJV.14: So Judah and his brothers came to Joseph’s house, and he was still there; and they fell before him on the ground.
NKJV.15: And Joseph said to them, “What deed is this you have done? Did you not know that such a man as I can certainly practice divination?”
NKJV.16: Then Judah said, “What shall we say to my lord? What shall we speak? Or how shall we clear ourselves? God has found out the iniquity of your servants; here we are, my lord’s slaves, both we and he also with whom the cup was found.”
NKJV.17: But he said, “Far be it from me that I should do so; the man in whose hand the cup was found, he shall be my slave. And as for you, go up in peace to your father.”
NKJV.18: Then Judah came near to him and said: “O my lord, please let your servant speak a word in my lord’s hearing, and do not let your anger burn against your servant; for you are even like Pharaoh.
NKJV.19: My lord asked his servants, saying, ‘Have you a father or a brother?’
NKJV.20: And we said to my lord, ‘We have a father, an old man, and a child of his old age, who is young; his brother is dead, and he alone is left of his mother’s children, and his father loves him.’
NKJV.21: Then you said to your servants, ‘Bring him down to me, that I may set my eyes on him.’
NKJV.22: And we said to my lord, ‘The lad cannot leave his father, for if he should leave his father, his father would die.’
NKJV.23: But you said to your servants, ‘Unless your youngest brother comes down with you, you shall see my face no more.’
NKJV.24: “So it was, when we went up to your servant my father, that we told him the words of my lord.
NKJV.25: And our father said, ‘Go back and buy us a little food.’
NKJV.26: But we said, ‘We cannot go down; if our youngest brother is with us, then we will go down; for we may not see the man’s face unless our youngest brother is with us.’
NKJV.27: Then your servant my father said to us, ‘You know that my wife bore me two sons;
NKJV.28: and the one went out from me, and I said, “Surely he is torn to pieces”; and I have not seen him since.
NKJV.29: But if you take this one also from me, and calamity befalls him, you shall bring down my gray hair with sorrow to the grave.’
NKJV.30: “Now therefore, when I come to your servant my father, and the lad is not with us, since his life is bound up in the lad’s life,
NKJV.31: it will happen, when he sees that the lad is not with us, that he will die. So your servants will bring down the gray hair of your servant our father with sorrow to the grave.
NKJV.32: For your servant became surety for the lad to my father, saying, ‘If I do not bring him back to you, then I shall bear the blame before my father forever.’
NKJV.33: Now therefore, please let your servant remain instead of the lad as a slave to my lord, and let the lad go up with his brothers.
NKJV.34: For how shall I go up to my father if the lad is not with me, lest perhaps I see the evil that would come upon my father?”

ESV.1: Then he commanded the steward of his house, “Fill the men's sacks with food, as much as they can carry, and put each man's money in the mouth of his sack,
ESV.2: and put my cup, the silver cup, in the mouth of the sack of the youngest, with his money for the grain.” And he did as Joseph told him.
ESV.3: As soon as the morning was light, the men were sent away with their donkeys.
ESV.4: They had gone only a short distance from the city. Now Joseph said to his steward, “Up, follow after the men, and when you overtake them, say to them, ‘Why have you repaid evil for good?
ESV.5: Is it not from this that my lord drinks, and by this that he practices divination? You have done evil in doing this.’”
ESV.6: When he overtook them, he spoke to them these words.
ESV.7: They said to him, “Why does my lord speak such words as these? Far be it from your servants to do such a thing!
ESV.8: Behold, the money that we found in the mouths of our sacks we brought back to you from the land of Canaan. How then could we steal silver or gold from your lord's house?
ESV.9: Whichever of your servants is found with it shall die, and we also will be my lord's servants.”
ESV.10: He said, “Let it be as you say: he who is found with it shall be my servant, and the rest of you shall be innocent.”
ESV.11: Then each man quickly lowered his sack to the ground, and each man opened his sack.
ESV.12: And he searched, beginning with the eldest and ending with the youngest. And the cup was found in Benjamin's sack.
ESV.13: Then they tore their clothes, and every man loaded his donkey, and they returned to the city.
ESV.14: When Judah and his brothers came to Joseph's house, he was still there. They fell before him to the ground.
ESV.15: Joseph said to them, “What deed is this that you have done? Do you not know that a man like me can indeed practice divination?”
ESV.16: And Judah said, “What shall we say to my lord? What shall we speak? Or how can we clear ourselves? God has found out the guilt of your servants; behold, we are my lord's servants, both we and he also in whose hand the cup has been found.”
ESV.17: But he said, “Far be it from me that I should do so! Only the man in whose hand the cup was found shall be my servant. But as for you, go up in peace to your father.”
ESV.18: Then Judah went up to him and said, “Oh, my lord, please let your servant speak a word in my lord's ears, and let not your anger burn against your servant, for you are like Pharaoh himself.
ESV.19: My lord asked his servants, saying, ‘Have you a father, or a brother?’
ESV.20: And we said to my lord, ‘We have a father, an old man, and a young brother, the child of his old age. His brother is dead, and he alone is left of his mother's children, and his father loves him.’
ESV.21: Then you said to your servants, ‘Bring him down to me, that I may set my eyes on him.’
ESV.22: We said to my lord, ‘The boy cannot leave his father, for if he should leave his father, his father would die.’
ESV.23: Then you said to your servants, ‘Unless your youngest brother comes down with you, you shall not see my face again.’
ESV.24: “When we went back to your servant my father, we told him the words of my lord.
ESV.25: And when our father said, ‘Go again, buy us a little food,’
ESV.26: we said, ‘We cannot go down. If our youngest brother goes with us, then we will go down. For we cannot see the man's face unless our youngest brother is with us.’
ESV.27: Then your servant my father said to us, ‘You know that my wife bore me two sons.
ESV.28: One left me, and I said, “Surely he has been torn to pieces,” and I have never seen him since.
ESV.29: If you take this one also from me, and harm happens to him, you will bring down my gray hairs in evil to Sheol.’
ESV.30: “Now therefore, as soon as I come to your servant my father, and the boy is not with us, then, as his life is bound up in the boy's life,
ESV.31: as soon as he sees that the boy is not with us, he will die, and your servants will bring down the gray hairs of your servant our father with sorrow to Sheol.
ESV.32: For your servant became a pledge of safety for the boy to my father, saying, ‘If I do not bring him back to you, then I shall bear the blame before my father all my life.’
ESV.33: Now therefore, please let your servant remain instead of the boy as a servant to my lord, and let the boy go back with his brothers.
ESV.34: For how can I go back to my father if the boy is not with me? I fear to see the evil that would find my father.”

AMP.1: And he commanded the steward of his house, saying, "Fill the men's sacks with food, as much as they can carry, and put every man's [grain] money in the mouth of the sack.
AMP.2: Put my [personal] cup, the silver cup, in the mouth of the sack of the youngest, with his grain money." And the steward did as Joseph had told him.
AMP.3: As soon as the morning was light, the men were sent away, they and their donkeys.
AMP.4: When they had left the city, and were not yet far away, Joseph said to his steward, "Get up, follow after the men; and when you overtake them, say to them, 'Why have you repaid evil [to us] for good [paid to you]?
AMP.5: Is this not my lord's drinking cup and the one which he uses for divination? You have done [a great and unforgivable] wrong in doing this.'"
AMP.6: So the steward overtook them and he said these words to them.
AMP.7: They said to him, "Why does my lord speak these things? Far be it from your servants to do such a thing!
AMP.8: Please remember, the money which we found in the mouths of our sacks we have brought back to you from the land of Canaan. Is it likely then that we would steal silver or gold from your master's house?
AMP.9: With whomever of your servants your master's cup is found, let him die, and the rest of us will be my lord's slaves."
AMP.10: And the steward said, "Now let it be as you say; he with whom the cup is found will be my slave, but the rest of you shall be blameless."
AMP.11: Then every man quickly lowered his sack to the ground and each man opened his sack [confident the cup would not be found among them].
AMP.12: The steward searched, beginning with the eldest and ending with the youngest, and the cup was found in Benjamin's sack.
AMP.13: Then they tore their clothes [in grief]; and after each man had loaded his donkey again, they returned to the city.
AMP.14: When Judah and his brothers came to Joseph's house, he was still there; and they fell to the ground before him.
AMP.15: Joseph spoke harshly to them, "What is this thing that you have done? Do you not realize that such a man as I can indeed practice divination and foretell [everything you do without outside knowledge of it]?"
AMP.16: So Judah said, "What can we say to my lord? What can we reply? Or how can we clear ourselves, since God has exposed the sin and guilt of your servants? Behold, we are my lord's slaves, the rest of us as well as he with whom the cup is found."
AMP.17: But Joseph said, "Far be it from me that I should do that; but the man in whose hand the cup has been found, he will be my servant; and as for [the rest of] you, get up and go in peace to your father."
AMP.18: Then Judah approached him, and said, "O my lord, please let your servant say a word to you in private, and do not let your anger blaze against your servant, for you are equal to Pharaoh [so I speak as if directly to him].
AMP.19: My lord asked his servants, saying, 'Have you a father or a brother?'
AMP.20: We said to my lord, 'We have an old father and a young [brother, Benjamin, the] child of his old age. Now his brother [Joseph] is dead, and he alone is left of [the two sons born of] his mother, and his father loves him.'
AMP.21: Then you said to your servants, 'Bring him down to me that I may actually see him.'
AMP.22: But we said to my lord, 'The young man cannot leave his father, for if he should leave his father, his father would die.'
AMP.23: You said to your servants, 'Unless your youngest brother comes with you, you shall not see my face again.'
AMP.24: So when we went back to your servant my father, we told him what my lord had said.
AMP.25: Our father said, 'Go back [to Egypt], and buy us a little food.'
AMP.26: But we said, 'We cannot go down [to Egypt]. If our youngest brother is with us, then we will go down [there]; for we [were sternly told that we] cannot see the man's face unless our youngest brother is with us.'
AMP.27: Your servant my father said to us, 'You know that my wife [Rachel] bore me [only] two sons.
AMP.28: And one [son] went out from me, and I said, "Surely he is torn to pieces," and I have not seen him since.
AMP.29: If you take this one also from me, and harm or an accident happens to him, you will bring my gray hair down to Sheol in sorrow.'
AMP.30: Now, therefore, when I come to your servant my father, and the young man is not with us, since his life is bound up in the young man's life,
AMP.31: when he sees that the young man is not with us, he will die; and your servants will bring the gray hair of your servant our father down to Sheol in [great] sorrow.
AMP.32: For your servant became security for the young man to my father, saying, 'If I do not bring him back to you, then let me bear the blame before my father forever.'
AMP.33: Now, therefore, please let your servant (Judah) remain here instead of the youth [to be] a slave to my lord, and let the young man go home with his brothers.
AMP.34: How can I go up to my father if the young man is not with me—for fear that I would see the tragedy that would overtake my [elderly] father [if Benjamin does not return]?"

CSB17.7: They said to him, “Why does my lord say these things? Your servants could not possibly do such a thing.

CSB17.9: If it is found with one of us, your servants, he must die, and the rest of us will become my lord’s slaves.” <sup>ⓐ</sup>

CSB17.11: So each one quickly lowered his sack to the ground and opened it.
CSB17.12: The steward searched, beginning with the oldest and ending with the youngest, and the cup was found in Benjamin’s sack.

CSB17.14: When Judah and his brothers reached Joseph’s house, he was still there. They fell to the ground before him. <sup>ⓒ</sup>

CSB17.16: “What can we say to my lord?” Judah replied. “How can we plead? How can we justify ourselves? God has exposed your servants’ iniquity. We are now my lord’s slaves — both we and the one in whose possession the cup was found.”
CSB17.17: Then Joseph said, “I swear that I will not do this. The man in whose possession the cup was found will be my slave. The rest of you can go in peace to your father.”
CSB17.18: But Judah approached him and said, “My lord, please let your servant speak personally to my lord. <sup>[1]</sup> Do not be angry with your servant, for you are like Pharaoh. <sup>ⓓ</sup>
CSB17.19: My lord asked his servants, ‘Do you have a father or a brother?’
CSB17.20: and we answered my lord, ‘We have an elderly father and a younger brother, the child of his old age. <sup>ⓔ</sup> The boy’s brother is dead. He is the only one of his mother’s sons left, and his father loves him.’
CSB17.21: Then you said to your servants, ‘Bring him to me so that I can see him.’ <sup>ⓕ</sup>
CSB17.22: But we said to my lord, ‘The boy cannot leave his father. If he were to leave, his father would die.’
CSB17.23: Then you said to your servants, ‘If your younger brother does not come down with you, you will not see me again.’ <sup>ⓖ</sup>
CSB17.24: “This is what happened when we went back to your servant my father: We reported to him the words of my lord.
CSB17.25: But our father said, ‘Go again, and buy us a little food.’ <sup>ⓗ</sup>
CSB17.26: We told him, ‘We cannot go down unless our younger brother goes with us. If our younger brother isn’t with us, we cannot see the man.’
CSB17.27: Your servant my father said to us, ‘You know that my wife bore me two sons.
CSB17.28: One is gone from me — I said he must have been torn to pieces — and I have never seen him again. <sup>ⓘ</sup>
CSB17.29: If you also take this one from me and anything happens to him, you will bring my gray hairs down to Sheol in sorrow.’ <sup>ⓙ</sup>
CSB17.30: “So if I come to your servant my father and the boy is not with us — his life is wrapped up with the boy’s life —
CSB17.31: when he sees that the boy is not with us, he will die. Then your servants will have brought the gray hairs of your servant our father down to Sheol in sorrow.
CSB17.32: Your servant became accountable to my father for the boy, saying, ‘If I do not return him to you, I will always bear the guilt for sinning against you, my father.’ <sup>ⓚ</sup>
CSB17.33: Now please let your servant remain here as my lord’s slave, in place of the boy. Let him go back with his brothers.
CSB17.34: For how can I go back to my father without the boy? I could not bear to see the grief that would overwhelm my father.”

NLT.1: When his brothers were ready to leave, Joseph gave these instructions to his palace manager: “Fill each of their sacks with as much grain as they can carry, and put each man’s money back into his sack.
NLT.2: Then put my personal silver cup at the top of the youngest brother’s sack, along with the money for his grain.” So the manager did as Joseph instructed him.
NLT.3: The brothers were up at dawn and were sent on their journey with their loaded donkeys.
NLT.4: But when they had gone only a short distance and were barely out of the city, Joseph said to his palace manager, “Chase after them and stop them. When you catch up with them, ask them, ‘Why have you repaid my kindness with such evil?
NLT.5: Why have you stolen my master’s silver cup, which he uses to predict the future? What a wicked thing you have done!’”
NLT.6: When the palace manager caught up with the men, he spoke to them as he had been instructed.
NLT.7: “What are you talking about?” the brothers responded. “We are your servants and would never do such a thing!
NLT.8: Didn’t we return the money we found in our sacks? We brought it back all the way from the land of Canaan. Why would we steal silver or gold from your master’s house?
NLT.9: If you find his cup with any one of us, let that man die. And all the rest of us, my lord, will be your slaves.”
NLT.10: “That’s fair,” the man replied. “But only the one who stole the cup will be my slave. The rest of you may go free.”
NLT.11: They all quickly took their sacks from the backs of their donkeys and opened them.
NLT.12: The palace manager searched the brothers’ sacks, from the oldest to the youngest. And the cup was found in Benjamin’s sack!
NLT.13: When the brothers saw this, they tore their clothing in despair. Then they loaded their donkeys again and returned to the city.
NLT.14: Joseph was still in his palace when Judah and his brothers arrived, and they fell to the ground before him.
NLT.15: “What have you done?” Joseph demanded. “Don’t you know that a man like me can predict the future?”
NLT.16: Judah answered, “Oh, my lord, what can we say to you? How can we explain this? How can we prove our innocence? God is punishing us for our sins. My lord, we have all returned to be your slaves — all of us, not just our brother who had your cup in his sack.”
NLT.17: “No,” Joseph said. “I would never do such a thing! Only the man who stole the cup will be my slave. The rest of you may go back to your father in peace.”
NLT.18: Then Judah stepped forward and said, “Please, my lord, let your servant say just one word to you. Please, do not be angry with me, even though you are as powerful as Pharaoh himself.
NLT.19: “My lord, previously you asked us, your servants, ‘Do you have a father or a brother?’
NLT.20: And we responded, ‘Yes, my lord, we have a father who is an old man, and his youngest son is a child of his old age. His full brother is dead, and he alone is left of his mother’s children, and his father loves him very much.’
NLT.21: “And you said to us, ‘Bring him here so I can see him with my own eyes.’
NLT.22: But we said to you, ‘My lord, the boy cannot leave his father, for his father would die.’
NLT.23: But you told us, ‘Unless your youngest brother comes with you, you will never see my face again.’
NLT.24: “So we returned to your servant, our father, and told him what you had said.
NLT.25: Later, when he said, ‘Go back again and buy us more food,’
NLT.26: we replied, ‘We can’t go unless you let our youngest brother go with us. We’ll never get to see the man’s face unless our youngest brother is with us.’
NLT.27: “Then my father said to us, ‘As you know, my wife had two sons,
NLT.28: and one of them went away and never returned. Doubtless he was torn to pieces by some wild animal. I have never seen him since.
NLT.29: Now if you take his brother away from me, and any harm comes to him, you will send this grieving, white-haired man to his grave. ’
NLT.30: “And now, my lord, I cannot go back to my father without the boy. Our father’s life is bound up in the boy’s life.
NLT.31: If he sees that the boy is not with us, our father will die. We, your servants, will indeed be responsible for sending that grieving, white-haired man to his grave.
NLT.32: My lord, I guaranteed to my father that I would take care of the boy. I told him, ‘If I don’t bring him back to you, I will bear the blame forever.’
NLT.33: “So please, my lord, let me stay here as a slave instead of the boy, and let the boy return with his brothers.
NLT.34: For how can I return to my father if the boy is not with me? I couldn’t bear to see the anguish this would cause my father!”

NET.20: We said to my lord, ‘We have an aged father, and there is a young boy who was born when our father was old. The boy’s brother is dead. He is the only one of his mother’s sons left, and his father loves him.’
NET.21: “Then you told your servants, ‘Bring him down to me so I can see him.’
NET.22: We said to my lord, ‘The boy cannot leave his father. If he leaves his father, his father will die.’
NET.23: But you said to your servants, ‘If your youngest brother does not come down with you, you will not see my face again.’
NET.24: When we returned to your servant my father, we told him the words of my lord.
NET.25: “Then our father said, ‘Go back and buy us a little food.’
NET.26: But we replied, ‘We cannot go down there. If our youngest brother is with us, then we will go, for we won’t be permitted to see the man’s face if our youngest brother is not with us.’
NET.27: “Then your servant my father said to us, ‘You know that my wife gave me two sons.
NET.28: The first disappeared and I said, “He has surely been torn to pieces.” I have not seen him since.
NET.29: If you take this one from me too and an accident happens to him, then you will bring down my gray hair in tragedy to the grave.’
NET.30: “So now, when I return to your servant my father, and the boy is not with us — his very life is bound up in his son’s life.
NET.31: When he sees the boy is not with us, he will die, and your servants will bring down the gray hair of your servant our father in sorrow to the grave.
NET.32: Indeed, your servant pledged security for the boy with my father, saying, ‘If I do not bring him back to you, then I will bear the blame before my father all my life.’
NET.33: “So now, please let your servant remain as my lord’s slave instead of the boy. As for the boy, let him go back with his brothers.
NET.34: For how can I go back to my father if the boy is not with me? I couldn’t bear to see my father’s pain.”

NRSVCE.1: Then he commanded the steward of his house, “Fill the men’s sacks with food, as much as they can carry, and put each man’s money in the top of his sack.
NRSVCE.2: Put my cup, the silver cup, in the top of the sack of the youngest, with his money for the grain.” And he did as Joseph told him.
NRSVCE.3: As soon as the morning was light, the men were sent away with their donkeys.
NRSVCE.4: When they had gone only a short distance from the city, Joseph said to his steward, “Go, follow after the men; and when you overtake them, say to them, ‘Why have you returned evil for good? Why have you stolen my silver cup?
NRSVCE.5: Is it not from this that my lord drinks? Does he not indeed use it for divination? You have done wrong in doing this.’”
NRSVCE.6: When he overtook them, he repeated these words to them.
NRSVCE.7: They said to him, “Why does my lord speak such words as these? Far be it from your servants that they should do such a thing!
NRSVCE.8: Look, the money that we found at the top of our sacks, we brought back to you from the land of Canaan; why then would we steal silver or gold from your lord’s house?
NRSVCE.9: Should it be found with any one of your servants, let him die; moreover the rest of us will become my lord’s slaves.”
NRSVCE.10: He said, “Even so; in accordance with your words, let it be: he with whom it is found shall become my slave, but the rest of you shall go free.”
NRSVCE.11: Then each one quickly lowered his sack to the ground, and each opened his sack.
NRSVCE.12: He searched, beginning with the eldest and ending with the youngest; and the cup was found in Benjamin’s sack.
NRSVCE.13: At this they tore their clothes. Then each one loaded his donkey, and they returned to the city.
NRSVCE.14: Judah and his brothers came to Joseph’s house while he was still there; and they fell to the ground before him.
NRSVCE.15: Joseph said to them, “What deed is this that you have done? Do you not know that one such as I can practice divination?”
NRSVCE.16: And Judah said, “What can we say to my lord? What can we speak? How can we clear ourselves? God has found out the guilt of your servants; here we are then, my lord’s slaves, both we and also the one in whose possession the cup has been found.”
NRSVCE.17: But he said, “Far be it from me that I should do so! Only the one in whose possession the cup was found shall be my slave; but as for you, go up in peace to your father.”
NRSVCE.18: Then Judah stepped up to him and said, “O my lord, let your servant please speak a word in my lord’s ears, and do not be angry with your servant; for you are like Pharaoh himself.
NRSVCE.19: My lord asked his servants, saying, ‘Have you a father or a brother?’
NRSVCE.20: And we said to my lord, ‘We have a father, an old man, and a young brother, the child of his old age. His brother is dead; he alone is left of his mother’s children, and his father loves him.’
NRSVCE.21: Then you said to your servants, ‘Bring him down to me, so that I may set my eyes on him.’
NRSVCE.22: We said to my lord, ‘The boy cannot leave his father, for if he should leave his father, his father would die.’
NRSVCE.23: Then you said to your servants, ‘Unless your youngest brother comes down with you, you shall see my face no more.’
NRSVCE.24: When we went back to your servant my father we told him the words of my lord.
NRSVCE.25: And when our father said, ‘Go again, buy us a little food,’
NRSVCE.26: we said, ‘We cannot go down. Only if our youngest brother goes with us, will we go down; for we cannot see the man’s face unless our youngest brother is with us.’
NRSVCE.27: Then your servant my father said to us, ‘You know that my wife bore me two sons;
NRSVCE.28: one left me, and I said, Surely he has been torn to pieces; and I have never seen him since.
NRSVCE.29: If you take this one also from me, and harm comes to him, you will bring down my gray hairs in sorrow to Sheol.’
NRSVCE.30: Now therefore, when I come to your servant my father and the boy is not with us, then, as his life is bound up in the boy’s life,
NRSVCE.31: when he sees that the boy is not with us, he will die; and your servants will bring down the gray hairs of your servant our father with sorrow to Sheol.
NRSVCE.32: For your servant became surety for the boy to my father, saying, ‘If I do not bring him back to you, then I will bear the blame in the sight of my father all my life.’
NRSVCE.33: Now therefore, please let your servant remain as a slave to my lord in place of the boy; and let the boy go back with his brothers.
NRSVCE.34: For how can I go back to my father if the boy is not with me? I fear to see the suffering that would come upon my father.”
